questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university supplied us with a lot of information. It was actually almost too much information because it some times made it more confusing and stressfull to navigate in all the information and different deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university took very good care of us when we arrived. The communication was good - it was easy to get in touch with the orientation staff, and they were very helpful and accommodating.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through a housing Facebook group, and I can recommend checking out different Facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can take a while finding a good house. Do not compromise with the standard. Make sure you get a contract, and use your common sense.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a very old system, and you had to complete an immunization form and get the university's approval of the form before you could register for courses. This process put you in risk of not getting the courses you wanted/get waitlisted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A very long course material.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the approval of immunization before the registration opened, so I got waitlisted on almost all the courses that I wanted. But in the end I did get most of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have the approval of the immunization form (if required) before the registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did take both first year courses and three year courses. The level was moderate to difficult, but I think it depends on what courses you take - especially whether it is a completely new course for you or if you have taken a similar course in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures are similar, but the professors cold call the students a lot more at the host institution.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Torts, Corporate Finance and Legal Profession

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Torts - I had a good professor that made the classes fun and interesting. It was also interesting to compare the US tort system with the Danish.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation costs. If you don't have a car you will use Uber/Lyft a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could imagine - fitness center, swimming activities, pool, volleyball, basketball, american football, outdoor adventures, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go cheer on the university's sports teams - it is a fun and authentic american collage experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city you live in and travel around the states.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, but there are a lot of cultural differences that you have to meet with an open mind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to socialize with local students you must be the one taking the initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That it isn't safe to walk around in the evening/night because of high crime rates and gun policies in the US.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are fun and straightforward to strangers - that is very different from how it is in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) take advantage of the Professors and the staff - they are much more likely to help you than the KU staff. 2) meet the culture with an open mind. 3) make a list of all the deadlines to make sure you don't miss any of them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely to adapt into the new culture both socially and privately, but it has been an interesting challenge, and I have acquired a lot of personal experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
